audience: a parent who already chose a curriculum on purpose and wants the record kept, not a new curriculum
a parent teaching two or three children at one kitchen table whose records have started to blur together
a family in a state that asks for a notice, a log, a portfolio or a yearly evaluation, saving pins before the review
a first-year homeschooler, often starting mid-year, working out the paperwork order
a parent who writes on paper some weeks and on a phone other weeks, and wants both to count
a parent of a reluctant reader who keeps a reading list and wants it to stay gentle

visualWorld.setting: The kitchen-table classroom, drawn flat and from slightly above: an oak table with a few grain lines, the working pages of The Homeschool Year lying on it, a stack of picture books, pencils in a mug, a portfolio binder with divider tabs, a child's drawing pinned to a cork board or the fridge, and a phone propped against the books showing the real app. Everything is paper, pencil and a binder. It is a parent's desk, not a classroom and not a children's app.

props.draw: Wide rounded rectangle in warm oak (#d9c3a5) with three or four thin, slightly lighter grain strokes and a soft darker ellipse shadow under it. Seen from about 30 degrees above, so the far edge is narrower than the near edge. No legs needed when cropped.

Portrait cream sheet (#fbfaf7) with a 3.5 px plum spine bar along the top edge, a tiny uppercase plum eyebrow line, a serif title, a thin rule under it, then the page's own grid in light rules (#ddd8d0). Lies on the table rotated 2 to 4 degrees with a flat drop shadow. Handwritten entries drawn as Newsreader italic in pencil grey (#8a8478) or as wavy pencil scribble lines where no real words exist.
working-page with the title 'The reading log' and three columns separated by faint vertical rules: 'Book' (wide), 'Started', 'Finished or stopped'. Seventeen ruled rows. Entries in pencil.

working-page titled 'Days schooled': twelve rows, each a short underline on the left for the month, then sixteen small empty squares, then a short underline on the right for the running total. Ticks drawn as short plum check strokes inside some squares.
working-page titled 'The daily log' with four column heads 'Date', 'Subject', 'What we did', 'How it went', sixteen ruled rows and faint column rules.

working-page titled 'A week at a time': two short write lines at the top ('Week beginning', 'Who this is for'), then six small plum uppercase day labels 'Monday' to 'Friday' and 'Spare day', each with two write lines. The Spare day block is left empty and drawn with a dashed plum outline.
working-page titled 'Things worth remembering': seven entries, each a short date stub line on the left and a long line beside it, plus one more full-width line under.
working-page titled 'One subject, over a term' with labelled write blocks: 'Where we started', 'What we covered', 'What went well', 'What we are coming back to', 'Work kept, and where'.

working-page with a topic title (e.g. 'Multiplication'), eight numbered question lines, and its bottom quarter folded back behind itself: draw the fold as a lighter trapezoid with a diagonal crease shadow and the word 'Answers' upside down on the flap, so the key is visibly out of the child's sight.
Four rounded pills stacked or in a row: outline pills in plum-soft (#f1ebf2) with plum text, the one being argued for filled in plum (#6a4a72) with white text.

Clipboard (rounded rectangle board in kraft #c9a87a with a dark ink clip at the top) holding a sheet of short lines, each with a small square tick box on the left; ticked boxes carry a plum check stroke.

Open three-ring binder seen from above: two rectangles side by side (left cover plum #6a4a72 or kraft, right page cream), three ring circles on the spine, and five divider tabs sticking out of the right edge as small staggered rounded rectangles in plum-soft, plum-mid and cream, each with a numeral or a short label.

The real My Homeschool Record cover from printables/document.tsx: cream page, tiny plum uppercase 'Homeschooling Companion', seven thin plum lines of different lengths (one bolder), a heavy ink rule near the bottom, 'My Homeschool Record' in serif, and a plum-soft box with a plum left border at the foot.

The printed record's 'What your state asks for.' page: plum eyebrow '<State>, <Level> regulation', serif title, the state's one-line note, then rows each with a requirement label on the left and a small pill tag on the right, and a faint footer line.

visualWorld.palette: Paper first, plum second. Light cream ground (#fbfaf7 and #f5f1ea from the handbook), ink #1a1d24 for type, the product's own plum #6a4a72 with #4a3350 / #8e6f95 / #f1ebf2 / #f6f1f7 for the accent scale, and warm natural prop colours that sit beside plum without competing: oak #d9c3a5, kraft #c9a87a, cork #cfa77a, pencil ochre #d8a657, sage #a3b18a, dusty rose #d9a5a0, rule grey #ddd8d0 and pencil grey #8a8478. No primary reds, blues or yellows: the product definition says its colour must never read as children's software.
visualWorld.mood: Calm, bookish and lived-in. A real table on an ordinary Tuesday: a little untidy, honest, pencil-marked, never a staged classroom and never a cartoon. The pin should feel like a page a parent would actually fill in.

archetypes.name: The working page on the table
archetypes.clicks: Printable previews dominate homeschool record keeping, portfolio and reading log searches on Pinterest: the pin shows the page itself so the saver knows exactly what they get. Search results for record keeping forms, reading logs and attendance trackers are almost all page previews. Clean, readable, structured layouts are what Pinterest's own educator guidance says performs.
archetypes.layout: Ground: oak table filling the frame. Top band (y 60 to 330): headline in Newsreader, ink, left aligned at x 70, max 3 lines. Middle (y 360 to 1240): one working page, about 760 x 900, rotated 2 to 4 degrees, centred, with its real title and column heads legible; a pencil lies across its lower right and a mug or book stack overlaps the top left corner. Below the page (y 1260 to 1360): one sub line in Plex Sans. Foot (y 1390 to 1460): product line at bottom left (name and price, or 'Free guide'); bottom right kept clear for Pinterest's UI.
archetypes.visual: One real page from The Homeschool Year, drawn with its real structure (columns, rows, boxes), a few pencil entries, and two or three table props.
archetypes.text: Headline (the pin's title), the page's own printed title and column heads (from printables/handbook.tsx), pencil entries only where a guide or the handbook gives example words, and the sub line from the pin's own description.
archetypes.bestFor: Reading log, days schooled, daily log, things worth remembering, the full set of working pages, a first page.

archetypes.name: The state tile map
archetypes.clicks: The colour-coded state map of regulation levels (the HSLDA-style map reproduced by AOP, SheKnows and others) is the reference visual this audience already knows and saves. A map pin promises 'find your state' in one glance, which is the job a searcher has.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. Top (y 60 to 300): headline, centred, 2 to 3 lines. Middle (y 330 to 1000): the 51-square tile map, about 880 wide, centred. Under the map (y 1020 to 1110): the four-level legend in one row with counts. Lower band (y 1140 to 1360): either the sub line, or an inset card (a cropped real Kids screenshot or a drawn state page) overlapping the map's lower right with a pencil arrow to the picked state. Foot: 'Laws change. Confirm with your state.' in small grey, then the product line at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: Fifty-one squares filled by the level in HOMESCHOOL_STATE_REQUIREMENTS, with an optional picked state outlined in ink.
archetypes.text: Level names and counts computed from src/lib/homeschoolStateRequirements.ts (HOMESCHOOL_STATE_REQUIREMENTS); one state's real level and note when a state is picked; the caution line from the product's own copy.
archetypes.bestFor: Requirements by state, laws by state, 'pick your state', what your state asks you to keep.

archetypes.name: The portfolio binder
archetypes.clicks: Portfolio and evaluation content on Pinterest is built around the binder: tabbed dividers per subject or per child, a cover page, a list of what goes inside. Parents save it as the checklist they will assemble against, which is exactly the use evaluation-season pins get.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground with a strip of oak table across the lower half. Top (y 60 to 320): headline, left aligned. Middle (y 340 to 1200): open binder, about 900 wide, slightly rotated, divider tabs on the right edge; the right page carries the real content (a list, the record cover, the state page or the printed log). Optional second binder half behind it for two children. Bottom (y 1230 to 1360): sub line. Foot: product line at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: An open three-ring binder with labelled tabs and one real printed page from the product (record cover, state page, log page) or the guide's list of contents.
archetypes.text: Tab labels and list items copied from the portfolio, evaluation and record-keeping guides or from the printed record's real labels in printables/document.tsx and book.ts.
archetypes.bestFor: What goes in a portfolio, preparing for an evaluation, the printed record, what prints, more than one child, what to keep.

archetypes.name: Numbered index cards on the cork board
archetypes.clicks: 'How to start' and 'what to do first' content is searched as steps, and the beginner guides that rank are numbered step lists. Numbered, short, high-contrast phrases are what pin design guidance says readers absorb in the one second a scroll gives them. Cards on a board also look like a real family's planning wall.
archetypes.layout: Cork board fills the frame inside an oak frame. Top (y 60 to 300): headline on a cream paper strip taped across the board. Middle (y 330 to 1300): three to five index cards in a loose column or zigzag, each about 760 x 190, numbered 1 to 5 in large serif, each with one short line; the child's drawing pinned in one gap for warmth. Foot: product line on a small cream tag at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: Index cards with a big numeral and one line each, push pins and washi tape, a child's drawing pinned among them. Variants: two cards side by side for a comparison, or a staircase of cards for 'go back one step'.
archetypes.text: Each card is a step or rule copied from the pin's guide (its 'steps' or list items) or from handbookContent.ts METHOD sections. No paraphrase.
archetypes.bestFor: First-month paperwork order, notice of intent steps, what to change first, short-day list, evaluation evening, three columns of a reading log.

archetypes.name: The four-day week board
archetypes.clicks: Weekly schedules and planners are among the most saved homeschool printables, but nearly every one assumes Monday to Friday. A Pinterest search for four-day homeschool planners found none built for it, so a board with one deliberately empty day stands out in a feed full of five-column grids.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. Top (y 60 to 300): headline. Middle (y 330 to 1150): a wide week board, day columns Monday to Friday plus an empty 'Spare day' column, with subject tiles placed on the days the product's real weekday pattern puts them; or a wall calendar for month views. Under it (y 1170 to 1340): a short legend or the sub line. Foot: product line at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: Day columns with subject tiles, one day left visibly empty (dashed, hatched); or a wall calendar with ticked days; or one lane per child.
archetypes.text: Day names from the weekly plan page (printables/handbook.tsx), subject days from the four-day-week guide or from startingOutline.ts SHAPES with today.ts WEEKDAYS_BY_FREQUENCY, labels like 'Your curriculum' from learning.ts SOURCE_LABEL.
archetypes.bestFor: Four-day week, starting outline, wait a week, what counts as a school day, attendance in June, per-child today.

archetypes.name: The kitchen-table scene with the real app
archetypes.clicks: Pinterest's own creative guidance is to show the product in use, in a setting people recognise, so they can picture using it. A homeschool kitchen table is that setting for this audience, and the real screenshot on a phone propped against the books proves the product exists.
archetypes.layout: Full-bleed illustrated scene: wall at the top third (cork board, child's drawing, clock or calendar), table across the middle and lower half. Headline sits on the wall area (y 60 to 330), left aligned. The focal object (phone or laptop with a real screenshot, or the printed handbook) sits at the table's centre (y 600 to 1180), larger than everything else. Sub line in a cream band (y 1240 to 1360). Foot: product line at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: The kitchen table with books, mug, pencils and paper, and a phone or laptop carrying one of the three real screenshots; variants for morning, evening, three place settings, or a reading rug.
archetypes.text: Headline, the sub line from the description, and whatever words are on the real screenshot. Small labels on props only when they are copied from the pin's description or guide.
archetypes.bestFor: Product pins about Today, the record, choosing a curriculum stance, paper and screen, several children; catch-up evening; the reading corner.

archetypes.name: The parent's clipboard: check sheet and results
archetypes.clicks: Assessment pins in this niche are saved as ready-to-use question sheets; the folded answer key and the honest result labels show at a glance that this is a gentle check run at home, not a test, which is the reassurance 'gentle homeschooling' searchers look for.
archetypes.layout: Cream ground. Top (y 60 to 300): headline. Middle (y 330 to 1180): a clipboard holding a check sheet with eight numbered questions, its bottom folded back to hide 'Answers'; or a topic tick list. Right side or below (y 1000 to 1300): the four result pills stacked, the relevant one filled in plum. Foot: product line at bottom left.
archetypes.visual: Kraft clipboard, check sheet with real questions, folded answer flap, four result pills.
archetypes.text: Questions copied from CHECK_SHEETS in printables/handbookContent.ts, result labels from STANDING_LABEL in check.ts, topic names from TOPICS in taxonomy.ts.
archetypes.bestFor: Did it stick, how to check learning, not enough to say, tick what you are teaching.
